client.switcher.dialog_label.note: Accessible name of the client switcher dialog (FR-FRM-000).

client.switcher.search_label.note: Accessible name of the search input. Names all three things it searches, because the KvK number is the one people do not expect to work.
client.switcher.search_label.nl: Zoek klanten op naam, handelsnaam of KvK-nummer
client.switcher.search_label.en: Search clients by name, trade name or KvK number

client.switcher.list_label.note: Accessible name of the results listbox.

client.switcher.no_matches.note: Empty result set. {query} is what the person typed, quoted, so it is clear the search — not the account — is what came up empty.

client.switcher.kvk.note: The KvK number beside a client's name. Identical in both because KvK is a statutory term that keeps its Dutch form in the English UI (FR-LOC-001c) — 'Chamber of Commerce number' would leave an English-speaking owner unable to match what is on screen to what is on the paper in front of them. See glossary.json.

client.switcher.current.note: Marks the client the session already has open, so switching to it is visibly a no-op.

client.header.loading.note: FR-FRM-000a. Shown while GET /v1/switcher/active is still in flight — deliberately distinct from client.header.none_selected, which is only for a CONFIRMED absence of an active client. Showing 'no client selected' during this window would be a false negative at exactly the moment the requirement exists to prevent.

client.header.none_selected.note: FR-FRM-000a. Shown instead of an empty header when the session is inside no client — a blank space is indistinguishable from a header that failed to load.

client.header.colour_ambiguous.note: FR-FRM-000a. Another client in this user's switcher carries the same colour marker, so the colour is not distinguishing and the name is what to read.
client.header.colour_ambiguous.nl: Een andere klant heeft dezelfde kleur — controleer de naam
client.header.colour_ambiguous.en: Another client shares this colour — check the name
